expected_issues.title: `getMCPServerPrompts(serverName) || []` may hide a bug if the function can legitimately r…
expected_issues.description: `getMCPServerPrompts(serverName) || []` may hide a bug if the function can legitimately return `null/undefined` due to an error state. Consider returning a default empty array from `getMCPServerPrompts` itself (stronger API contract), or at least add a comment/guard if `undefined` indicates an exceptional condition.
expected_issues.source_text: `getMCPServerPrompts(serverName) || []` may hide a bug if the function can legitimately return `null/undefined` due to an error state. Consider returning a default empty array from `getMCPServerPrompts` itself (stronger API contract), or at least add a comment/guard if `undefined` indicates an exceptional condition.

expected_issues.title: `if (descLines)` is always truthy because `split('\n')` always returns an array
expected_issues.description:
`if (descLines)` is always truthy because `split('\n')` always returns an array. This makes the `else` branch effectively unreachable. If the intent is to handle empty/whitespace-only descriptions, check `descLines.length` and/or filter out empty lines before printing.

Also consider trimming and skipping empty lines to avoid printing blank green lines.
expected_issues.source_text:
`if (descLines)` is always truthy because `split('\n')` always returns an array. This makes the `else` branch effectively unreachable. If the intent is to handle empty/whitespace-only descriptions, check `descLines.length` and/or filter out empty lines before printing.

Also consider trimming and skipping empty lines to avoid printing blank green lines.

expected_issues.description: Potential command name collisions: using only `prompt.name` as the slash command name can conflict across multiple MCP servers or with existing built-ins. Consider namespacing (e.g., `${serverName}:${prompt.name}`) or adding a server-level parent command to avoid overriding/ambiguity in the CLI command registry.

Consider namespacing (e.g., `${serverName}:${prompt.name}`) or adding a server-level parent command to avoid overriding/ambiguity in the CLI command registry.

The `mcpClient` variable is declared without an explicit type annotation
expected_issues.description:
The `mcpClient` variable is declared without an explicit type annotation. Since `connectToMcpServer` returns `Promise<Client>`, the variable should be explicitly typed as `Client | null` for better type safety and code clarity.

```suggestion
            let mcpClient: Client | null = null;
```

Consider clearing prompts on successful disconnect paths as well (not only `onerror`) and/or providing an explicit cleanup API or size limit/TTL to avoid memory leaks in long-lived processes.

expected_issues.title: Error handling relies on substring matching `'Method not found'`, which is brittle across…
expected_issues.description: Error handling relies on substring matching `'Method not found'`, which is brittle across SDK versions/locales. Prefer checking structured error codes (e.g., JSON-RPC error code -32601) if available from the SDK, or narrow to a specific error type. Otherwise you may suppress real errors that happen to include the same phrase.
expected_issues.source_text: Error handling relies on substring matching `'Method not found'`, which is brittle across SDK versions/locales. Otherwise you may suppress real errors that happen to include the same phrase.
